newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU to tax daily soft wheat and durum - sources.
newsitem.headline: EU to tax daily soft wheat and durum - sources.

text.p: The European Union's cereals committee, which earlier restored wheat export taxes at a weekly tender, is expected to agree to widen taxes to the daily export channel for soft wheat and durum, grain industry sources said.

Details were unconfirmed as the panel continued its weekly meeting in Brussels, but industry sources said the committee was likely to impose a daily tax on soft wheat very close to the 0.5 Ecu minimum level awarded on a weekly basis earlier on Thursday.
Durum was likely to be taxed at around five Ecus, they said.
The daily channel offers licences of a fixed value, rather than the floating levels directed by bids at weekly tenders.
Open on a first-come-first-served basis, the daily export route has previously been shut through punitive levels of tax when EU wheat subsidies have gone into negative territory.

But traders noted the 0.50 Ecu tax under consideration for soft wheat was within the same commercial range as the weekly tender and was lower than the maximum tax of some two Ecus paid out at the tender itself.

Wheat currently has a "nil value" entry in the daily system, meaning licences can be taken at the Commission's discretion but only for a short 30-day validity and subject to further fluctuations before they are used for export.
